name: Syndromic Sensorineural Deafness Due to Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect
aliases: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency with Sensorineural Hearing Loss

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Demonstration of combined oxidative phosphorylation enzyme deficiency in muscle or fibroblasts
Presence of additional systemic manifestations such as neurological or muscular symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral sensorineural deafness plus biochemical evidence of combined oxidative phosphorylation defect
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Typically progressive and present from early childhood
searchTerms: hearing loss from nerve damage both ears

pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by biochemical assays in muscle biopsy or fibroblasts

rare.notes: Including diabetes mellitus or growth hormone deficiency

laboratory: Combined deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV in muscle biopsy
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI may show cerebral or cerebellar atrophy
Muscle MRI may reveal fatty infiltration
genetic: Mutations in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation components or assembly factors
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or multiple deletions may be present
other: Audiometric confirmation of sensorineural hearing loss
Muscle biopsy histology showing ragged red fibers or COX-negative fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Subacute necrotizing encephalopathy with characteristic MRI basal ganglia lesions
Isolated hearing loss without multisystem involvement
Absence of biochemical oxidative phosphorylation defects
Sensorineural deafness with ovarian dysgenesis in females
Genetic mutations distinct from combined oxidative phosphorylation defects

redFlags: Rapidly progressive sensorineural hearing loss in infancy or early childhood
Evidence of multisystem involvement including muscle weakness and lactic acidosis
Biochemical confirmation of combined oxidative phosphorylation enzyme deficiencies
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Hirano M, et al. Mitochondrial DNA mutations and mitochondrial diseases. Ann Neurol. 1997 Sep;42(3):439-50.
